429	    def _plan_route(
430	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
431	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
432	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
433	
434	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
435	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
436	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
437	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
438	        """
439	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
440	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)
441	
442	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
443	        for task in self.tasks.values():
444	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
445	                continue
446	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
447	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
448	                continue
449	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
450	            if route is None:
451	                robot.route = []
452	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
453	            else:
454	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
455	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
456	                robot.route = route
457	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
458	
459	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
460	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
461	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
462	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
463	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
464	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
465	                continue
466	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
467	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
468	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
469	                continue
470	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
471	            if route is None:
472	                robot.route = []
473	                continue
474	            robot.route = route
475	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
476	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)

479	    # Traffic conflicts and yielding

482	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
483	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
484	        cells: set[Position] = set()
485	        for robot in self.robots.values():
486	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
487	                cells.update(robot.route)
488	        return cells
489	
490	    def _safe_side_cells(
491	        self,
492	        robot: Robot,
493	        occupied: Mapping[Position, str],
494	        reserved: Mapping[Position, str],
495	        forbidden: Iterable[Position] = (),
496	    ) -> Iterator[Position]:
497	        """Adjacent cells *robot* may actually side-step onto this tick.
498	
499	        The very same safety rule backs every side-step decision -- an idle
500	        robot yielding for someone, a busy robot dodging a blocker itself, and
501	        the hypothetical leave checks behind a retreat -- so the shared
502	        conditions live exactly here. A cell qualifies only when it:
503	
504	        * lies inside the map with no obstacle (``GridMap.neighbors`` already
505	          skips anything else),
506	        * is held by no robot in the given (possibly hypothetical) layout,
507	        * was not reserved by a move that already happened this tick,
508	        * lies on no other robot's remaining route (the moving robot's own
509	          route is excluded), and
510	        * is not among *forbidden*: cells that are physically free but unsafe
511	          for the caller's scenario, such as the requester's own cell (a
512	          side-step there would swap the two robots within one tick) or the
513	          retreating requester's replanned path (parking there only moves the
514	          blockage onto a cell the requester must re-enter).
515	
516	        Neighbours are yielded in the deterministic ``GridMap.neighbors``
517	        order (up, left, right, down); callers keep their own selection rules.
518	        """
519	        blocked = set(forbidden)
520	        blocked.update(self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id))
521	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(robot.position):
522	            if cell in blocked or cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
523	                continue
524	            yield cell
525	
526	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
527	        self,
528	        blocker: Robot,
529	        requester: Robot,
530	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
531	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
532	    ) -> Position | None:
533	        """Free side-cell an idle blocker can yield to, or None.
534	
535	        The requester's own cell is forbidden (yielding onto it would swap the
536	        two robots within one tick); every other safety condition is shared via
537	        :meth:`_safe_side_cells`, so the blocker never trades one blockage for
538	        another. The first candidate in neighbour order wins.
539	        """
540	        return next(
541	            self._safe_side_cells(
542	                blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=(requester.position,)
543	            ),
544	            None,
545	        )
546	
547	    def _self_sidestep(
548	        self,
549	        robot: Robot,
550	        task: Task | None,
551	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
552	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
553	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
554	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
555	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
556	
557	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
558	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
559	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
560	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
561	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
562	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
563	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
564	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
565	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
566	        """
567	        if task is None or task.completed:
568	            return None
569	        destination = robot.route[0]
570	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
571	        if blocker_id is None:
572	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
573	        best: tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None = None
574	        best_length = 0
575	        # Candidates arrive in neighbour order (up, left, right, down), so the
576	        # first candidate of the minimum replanned length automatically keeps
577	        # that order as the tie break.
578	        for cell in self._safe_side_cells(robot, occupied, reserved):
579	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
580	            if route is None:
581	                continue
582	            if (
583	                blocker_id is not None
584	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
585	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
586	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
587	                )
588	            ):
589	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
590	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
591	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
592	                continue
593	            if best is None or len(route) < best_length:
594	                best = (cell, route)
595	                best_length = len(route)
596	        return best
597	
598	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
599	        self,
600	        robot: Robot,
601	        side: Position,
602	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
603	        blocker_id: str,
604	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
605	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
606	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
607	    ) -> bool:
608	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
609	
610	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
611	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
612	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
613	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
614	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
615	        never rejected here.
616	        """
617	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
618	            return False
619	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
620	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
621	            return False
622	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
623	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
624	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
625	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
626	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id
627	        # The requester only gets back onto its route by driving through these
628	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
629	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
630	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
631	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
632	        return not self._can_vacate(
633	            blocker,
634	            robot,
635	            hyp_occupied,
636	            reserved,
637	            frozenset({robot.robot_id}) | already_moved,
638	            blocked_path,
639	        )
640	
641	    def _can_vacate(
642	        self,
643	        blocker: Robot,
644	        requester: Robot,
645	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
646	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
647	        checking: frozenset[str],
648	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
649	    ) -> bool:
650	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
651	
652	        An idle blocker leaves only by yielding onto a safe side cell for the
653	        requesting robot; a busy blocker leaves by driving onto its next
654	        waypoint (possibly following a chain of robots that all move this tick)
655	        or by sidestepping onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by
656	        map unreachability never move. *checking* names robots whose leave
657	        check is already on the call stack, so a cyclic dependency (a head-on
658	        deadlock, or the requester itself) is not assumed resolvable.
659	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive back
660	        through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so such
661	        sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on the
662	        blocker's own route does).
663	        """
664	        if blocker.robot_id in checking:
665	            return False
666	        task = self.tasks[blocker.task_id] if blocker.task_id is not None else None
667	        if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
668	            return False
669	        if task is not None and not blocker.route:
670	            # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this tick;
671	            # it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
672	            return False
673	        if task is None:
674	            # Idle robots only ever move by yielding for a requester, and they
675	            # do so onto the first safe cell in neighbour order. When that
676	            # particular cell sits on the path the retreating requester must
677	            # re-enter, parking there only relocates the blockage instead of
678	            # clearing it, so it does not count as leaving.
679	            side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, requester, occupied, reserved)
680	            return side is not None and side not in blocked_path
681	        if blocker.route:
682	            ahead = blocker.route[0]
683	            if (
684	                self.grid.traversable(ahead)
685	                and ahead not in occupied
686	                and ahead not in reserved
687	            ):
688	                return True
689	            occupant_id = occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
690	            if (
691	                occupant_id is not None
692	                and occupant_id != blocker.robot_id
693	                and occupant_id not in checking
694	            ):
695	                # The blocker could follow the robot ahead once that robot
696	                # vacates its cell this same tick.
697	                if self._can_vacate(
698	                    self.robots[occupant_id],
699	                    requester,
700	                    occupied,
701	                    reserved,
702	                    checking | {blocker.robot_id},
703	                    blocked_path,
704	                ):
705	                    return True
706	        # Otherwise the blocker might sidestep onto a free side cell itself,
707	        # but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has to use --
708	        # parking there only moves the blockage.
709	        for side_cell in self._safe_side_cells(
710	            blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=blocked_path
711	        ):
712	            if self._plan_route(blocker, task, start=side_cell) is not None:
713	                return True
714	        return False
715	
716	    def _update_traffic_waits(
717	        self,
718	        waited: dict[str, str],
719	        moved_ids: frozenset[str],
720	    ) -> None:
721	        """Keep only waits that still hold once the tick's moves have settled.
722	
723	        *waited* maps every robot that stopped this tick purely because
724	        another robot held its next waypoint to the robot it saw there at the
725	        time; *moved_ids* names the robots that ended up moving. The mid-tick
726	        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
727	        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
728	        A record survives only when the robot neither moved nor paused and its
729	        next waypoint is occupied by another robot in the final layout; the
730	        reported blocker is whichever robot actually occupies that cell. Any
731	        other outcome -- the robot moved, its task paused, or the way ahead
732	        cleared -- deletes the entry. A wait that continues without a free tick
733	        in between keeps accumulating even when the blocker changes identity;
734	        once interrupted, a later blockage starts a fresh count at one.
735	        """
736	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
737	        surviving: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
738	        for robot_id in waited:
739	            if robot_id in moved_ids:
740	                continue
741	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
742	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
743	                continue
744	            task = self.tasks.get(robot.task_id) if robot.task_id is not None else None
745	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
746	                continue
747	            blocker_id = occupied.get(robot.route[0])
748	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot_id:
749	                continue
750	            entry = self._traffic_waits.get(robot_id)
751	            if entry is None:
752	                surviving[robot_id] = {"blocked_by": [blocker_id], "ticks": 1}
753	            else:
754	                surviving[robot_id] = {
755	                    "blocked_by": [blocker_id],
756	                    "ticks": int(entry["ticks"]) + 1,
757	                }
758	        self._traffic_waits = surviving
759	
760	    def _reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change(self) -> None:
761	        """Drop wait records an accepted map edit has invalidated.
762	
763	        A map change never moves a robot, so it can neither create a wait nor
764	        add to one; but it can end one. A robot whose task just paused on
765	        unreachability has no route left to wait on, and a robot whose
766	        replanned next cell is no longer held by the recorded blocker is not
767	        blocked by it anymore -- both records are removed. An entry whose
768	        robot still faces the very same blocker on its refreshed route keeps
769	        its count untouched, whatever else the edit changed.
770	        """
771	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
772	        for robot_id, entry in list(self._traffic_waits.items()):
773	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
774	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
775	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
776	                continue
777	            if occupied.get(robot.route[0]) not in entry["blocked_by"]:
778	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
779	
780	    def _traffic_wait_report(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
781	        return [
782	            {
783	                "robot_id": robot_id,
784	                "blocked_by": list(entry["blocked_by"]),
785	                "ticks": entry["ticks"],
786	            }
787	            for robot_id, entry in sorted(self._traffic_waits.items())
788	        ]

790	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
791	    # Normal execution
792	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
793	
794	    def assign_tasks(self) -> None:
795	        """Assign pending tasks to the nearest idle robot using stable tie breaks."""
796	        pending = [task for task in self.tasks.values() if task.assigned_robot is None]
797	        for task in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: item.task_id):
798	            choices: list[tuple[int, str, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = []
799	            for robot in self.robots.values():
800	                if not robot.idle:
801	                    continue
802	                route = _plan_task_route(self.grid, robot.position, task)
803	                if route is None:
804	                    continue
805	                choices.append((len(route), robot.robot_id, route))
806	            if not choices:
807	                # No robot can reach this task yet; it keeps waiting and does
808	                # not block assignment of other tasks.
809	                continue
810	            _, robot_id, route = min(choices)
811	            robot = self.robots[robot_id]
812	            robot.task_id = task.task_id
813	            robot.route = route
814	            task.assigned_robot = robot_id
815	
816	    def _confirm_pickups(self) -> None:
817	        """A robot starting a tick on its pickup point collects first."""
818	        for robot in self.robots.values():
819	            if robot.task_id is None:
820	                continue
821	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
822	            if not task.completed and not task.picked_up and robot.position == task.pickup:
823	                task.picked_up = True
824	
825	    def step(self) -> dict[str, object]:
826	        self._confirm_pickups()
827	        self._recover_paused_tasks()
828	        self.assign_tasks()
829	        # A robot assigned while already standing on the pickup cell collects
830	        # immediately instead of driving off without the goods.
831	        self._confirm_pickups()
832	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
833	        reserved: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {}
834	        moved: list[str] = []
835	        moved_ids: set[str] = set()
836	        blocked_by: dict[str, str] = {}
837	
838	        def relocate(robot: Robot, destination: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
839	            del occupied[robot.position]
840	            robot.position = destination
841	            robot.distance_travelled += 1
842	            occupied[destination] = robot.robot_id
843	            reserved[destination] = robot.robot_id
844	            moved.append(robot.robot_id)
845	            moved_ids.add(robot.robot_id)
846	
847	        for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id):
848	            if robot.robot_id in moved_ids:
849	                # Already yielded this tick at another robot's request.
850	                continue
851	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id] if robot.task_id is not None else None
852	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
853	                # Paused by map unreachability: stays put, never yields.
854	                continue
855	            if not robot.route:
856	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
857	                continue
858	            destination = robot.route[0]
859	            if not self.grid.traversable(destination):
860	                # Defensive: routes are normally replanned on every map edit.
861	                if task is not None and not task.completed:
862	                    route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
863	                    if route is None:
864	                        robot.route = []
865	                        self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
866	                    else:
867	                        robot.route = route
868	                continue
869	            blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
870	            if blocker_id is None:
871	                blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
872	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot.robot_id:
873	                relocate(robot, destination)
874	                robot.route.pop(0)
875	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
876	                continue
877	            # Another robot is in the way; this is distinct from a
878	            # map-unreachability pause and the task stays active.
879	            blocker = self.robots[blocker_id]
880	            if blocker_id not in moved_ids:
881	                if blocker.task_id is None:
882	                    # Idle blocker: ask it to yield onto a free side cell,
883	                    # then take over the cell it vacated.
884	                    side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, robot, occupied, reserved)
885	                    if side is not None:
886	                        relocate(blocker, side)
887	                        relocate(robot, destination)
888	                        robot.route.pop(0)
889	                        self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
890	                        continue
891	                elif blocker.route:
892	                    ahead = blocker.route[0]
893	                    if (
894	                        self.grid.traversable(ahead)
895	                        and ahead not in occupied
896	                        and ahead not in reserved
897	                    ):
898	                        # The blocker is expected to drive on within this
899	                        # tick, so waiting one tick is cheaper than detouring.
900	                        blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
901	                        continue
902	            # The blocker cannot or will not move this tick: try to sidestep
903	            # onto a free adjacent cell and replan from there.
904	            side = self._self_sidestep(
905	                robot, task, occupied, reserved, frozenset(moved_ids)
906	            )
907	            if side is not None:
908	                cell, route = side
909	                relocate(robot, cell)
910	                robot.route = route
911	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
912	                continue
913	            blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
914	        self._update_traffic_waits(blocked_by, frozenset(moved_ids))
915	        self.tick += 1
916	        event: dict[str, object] = {
917	            "type": "tick",
918	            "tick": self.tick,
919	            "moved": moved,
920	            "robots": {robot_id: list(robot.position) for robot_id, robot in sorted(self.robots.items())},
921	            "completed": sorted(task.task_id for task in self.tasks.values() if task.completed),
922	        }
923	        self.replay.append(event)
924	        return event

926	    def _finish_if_arrived(self, robot: Robot) -> None:
927	        if robot.task_id is None:
928	            return
929	        task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
930	        if task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
931	            return
932	        if robot.position == task.pickup:
933	            task.picked_up = True
934	        if task.picked_up and robot.position == task.dropoff and not robot.route:
935	            task.completed = True
936	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
937	            robot.task_id = None

979	    def save_checkpoint(self, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> None:
980	        """Write the simulator state to *path* without changing this instance.
981	
982	        The write is atomic: an existing destination keeps either its complete
983	        old contents or the complete new contents, and a brand-new destination
984	        is either fully created or left absent. Filesystem or permission errors
985	        raise :class:`OSError`.
986	        """
987	        document = {
988	            "version": CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
989	            "grid": {
990	                "width": self.grid.width,
991	                "height": self.grid.height,
992	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.grid.obstacles)],
993	            },
994	            "base_grid": {
995	                "width": self.base_grid.width,
996	                "height": self.base_grid.height,
997	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.base_grid.obstacles)],
998	            },
999	            "tick": self.tick,
1000	            "robots": [
1001	                {
1002	                    "robot_id": robot.robot_id,
1003	                    "position": list(robot.position),
1004	                    "route": [list(cell) for cell in robot.route],
1005	                    "task_id": robot.task_id,
1006	                    "distance_travelled": robot.distance_travelled,
1007	                }
1008	                for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id)
1009	            ],
1010	            "tasks": [
1011	                {
1012	                    "task_id": task.task_id,
1013	                    "pickup": list(task.pickup),
1014	                    "dropoff": list(task.dropoff),
1015	                    "assigned_robot": task.assigned_robot,
1016	                    "picked_up": task.picked_up,
1017	                    "completed": task.completed,
1018	                }
1019	                for task in sorted(self.tasks.values(), key=lambda item: item.task_id)
1020	            ],
1021	            "replay": copy.deepcopy(self.replay),
1022	            "map_changes": copy.deepcopy(self.map_changes),
1023	            "paused_tasks": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
1024	            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
1025	        }
1026	        payload = (json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
1027	
1028	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(os.fspath(path))) or os.curdir
1029	        fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".checkpoint-", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory)
1030	        try:
1031	            handle = os.fdopen(fd, "wb")
1032	            try:
1033	                handle.write(payload)
1034	                handle.flush()
1035	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
1036	            finally:
1037	                handle.close()
1038	            os.replace(tmp_name, path)
1039	            self._fsync_directory(directory)
1040	        except BaseException:
1041	            # After a successful replace the temp name is already gone.
1042	            try:
1043	                os.unlink(tmp_name)
1044	            except OSError:
1045	                pass
1046	            raise

1048	    @staticmethod
1049	    def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
1050	        try:
1051	            dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
1052	        except OSError:
1053	            return
1054	        try:
1055	            os.fsync(dir_fd)
1056	        except OSError:
1057	            pass
1058	        finally:
1059	            os.close(dir_fd)

1061	    @classmethod
1062	    def load_checkpoint(cls, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> FleetSimulator:
1063	        """Load an independent simulator instance from *path*.
1064	
1065	        The returned simulator shares no mutable state with the file or any
1066	        other loaded instance. Invalid checkpoint content raises
1067	        :class:`ValueError` explaining the reason; read/permission failures
1068	        propagate as :class:`OSError`.
1069	        """
1070	        try:
1071	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
1072	                text = handle.read()
1073	        except OSError:
1074	            raise
1075	        try:
1076	            data = json.loads(text)
1077	        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
1078	            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint is not valid JSON: {exc.msg}") from exc
1079	        return cls._from_checkpoint(data)

1081	    @classmethod
1082	    def _from_checkpoint(cls, data: object) -> FleetSimulator:
1083	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
1084	            raise ValueError("checkpoint root must be a JSON object")
1085	
1086	        version = data.get("version")
1087	        if not _is_int(version):
1088	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'version' must be an integer")
1089	        if version not in _SUPPORTED_VERSIONS:
1090	            raise ValueError(
1091	                f"unsupported checkpoint version {version}; supported versions: "
1092	                f"{sorted(_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS)}"
1093	            )
1094	
1095	        grid = cls._load_grid(data)
1096	        tick = cls._load_tick(data)
1097	        robot_records, task_records = cls._load_entities(data)
1098	
1099	        map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1100	        paused: set[str] = set()
1101	        if version == 1:
1102	            replay = cls._load_legacy_replay(data)
1103	            base_grid = grid
1104	        else:
1105	            replay = cls._load_replay(data)
1106	            map_changes = cls._load_map_changes(data)
1107	            paused = cls._load_paused_tasks(data)
1108	            base_grid = cls._load_base_grid(data)
1109	            if (base_grid.width, base_grid.height) != (grid.width, grid.height):
1110	                raise ValueError("base grid dimensions must match the current grid")
1111	            cls._validate_map_history(base_grid, grid, map_changes)
1112	
1113	        robots: list[Robot] = []
1114	        for record in robot_records:
1115	            position = _as_pair(record["position"], f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position")
1116	            if not grid.traversable(position):
1117	                raise ValueError(
1118	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position {list(position)} is outside "
1119	                    "the map or inside an obstacle"
1120	                )
1121	            route: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
1122	            previous = position
1123	            for index, cell in enumerate(record["route"]):
1124	                waypoint = _as_pair(
1125	                    cell, f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {index}"
1126	                )
1127	                if not grid.traversable(waypoint):
1128	                    raise ValueError(
1129	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {list(waypoint)} is "
1130	                        "outside the map or inside an obstacle"
1131	                    )
1132	                if abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0]) + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1]) != 1:
1133	                    raise ValueError(
1134	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
1135	                        f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
1136	                    )
1137	                route.append(waypoint)
1138	                previous = waypoint
1139	            distance = record["distance_travelled"]
1140	            if not _is_int(distance) or distance < 0:
1141	                raise ValueError(
1142	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} distance_travelled must be a "
1143	                    "non-negative integer"
1144	                )
1145	            robots.append(Robot(record["robot_id"], position, route, record["task_id"], distance))
1146	
1147	        tasks: list[Task] = []
1148	        for record in task_records:
1149	            pickup = _as_pair(record["pickup"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} pickup")
1150	            dropoff = _as_pair(record["dropoff"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} dropoff")
1151	            tasks.append(
1152	                Task(
1153	                    record["task_id"],
1154	                    pickup,
1155	                    dropoff,
1156	                    record["assigned_robot"],
1157	                    record["picked_up"],
1158	                    record["completed"],
1159	                )
1160	            )
1161	
1162	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
1163	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
1164	
1165	        # Ownership is judged with the exact rules direct construction uses:
1166	        # mutual bindings for work in progress, historical owners for finished
1167	        # tasks, and a collected task that may never lack its carrier.
1168	        cls._validate_task_ownership(robots, tasks)
1169	        for task in tasks:
1170	            if task.completed and not task.picked_up:
1171	                raise ValueError(
1172	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is completed but never picked up"
1173	                )
1174	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
1175	                # Direct construction never sees a finished task without a
1176	                # historical owner because it cannot create completion itself,
1177	                # but a checkpoint document can spell one, and the running
1178	                # simulator only ever saves picked-up tasks with a carrier.
1179	                raise ValueError(
1180	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
1181	                )
1182	
1183	        cls._validate_paused_state(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id, grid)
1184	        cls._validate_active_task_routes(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id)
1185	        traffic_waits = cls._load_traffic_waits(data, robot_by_id)
1186	
1187	        replay_change_frames = cls._replay_map_change_frames(replay)
1188	        if replay_change_frames != map_changes:
1189	            raise ValueError("replay map-change frames do not match 'map_changes' history")
1190	
1191	        simulator = cls(grid, robots, tasks)
1192	        simulator.base_grid = base_grid
1193	        simulator.tick = tick
1194	        simulator.replay = copy.deepcopy(replay)
1195	        simulator.map_changes = copy.deepcopy(map_changes)
1196	        simulator._map_sequence = len(map_changes)
1197	        simulator.paused_tasks = set(paused)
1198	        simulator._traffic_waits = traffic_waits
1199	        # Version 1 has no edit history: its saved grid is the baseline and
1200	        # applies to every tick frame. Version 2 replays the recorded changes
1201	        # alongside the frames so each frame is judged against its contemporary
1202	        # map.
1203	        cls._validate_replay_positions(replay, tick, robot_by_id, base_grid, map_changes)
1204	        cls._validate_replay_completion(replay, tick, task_by_id)
1205	        return simulator

1213	    @classmethod
1214	    def _load_grid(cls, data: Mapping[str, object]) -> GridMap:
1215	        raw = cls._require_field(data, "grid")
1216	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
1217	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'grid' must be an object")
1218	        width = raw.get("width")
1219	        height = raw.get("height")
1220	        if not _is_int(width) or width <= 0:
1221	            raise ValueError("checkpoint grid width must be a positive integer")
1222	        if not _is_int(height) or height <= 0:
1223	            raise ValueError("checkpoint grid height must be a positive integer")
1224	        raw_obstacles = raw.get("obstacles")
1225	        if not isinstance(raw_obstacles, list):
1226	            raise ValueError("checkpoint grid 'obstacles' must be a list")
1227	        obstacles: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
1228	        for index, cell in enumerate(raw_obstacles):
1229	            obstacle = _as_pair(cell, f"obstacle entry {index}")
1230	            if not (0 <= obstacle[0] < width and 0 <= obstacle[1] < height):
1231	                raise ValueError(f"obstacle {list(obstacle)} lies outside the map")
1232	            obstacles.add(obstacle)
1233	        try:
1234	            return GridMap(width, height, frozenset(obstacles))
1235	        except ValueError as exc:
1236	            raise ValueError(f"invalid checkpoint grid: {exc}") from exc

1270	    @classmethod
1271	    def _load_entities(
1272	        cls, data: Mapping[str, object]
1273	    ) -> tuple[list[dict[str, object]], list[dict[str, object]]]:
1274	        raw_robots = cls._require_field(data, "robots")
1275	        raw_tasks = cls._require_field(data, "tasks")
1276	        if not isinstance(raw_robots, list):
1277	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'robots' must be a list")
1278	        if not isinstance(raw_tasks, list):
1279	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'tasks' must be a list")
1280	
1281	        robot_records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1282	        robot_ids: set[str] = set()
1283	        for index, record in enumerate(raw_robots):
1284	            if not isinstance(record, dict):
1285	                raise ValueError(f"robot entry {index} must be an object")
1286	            robot_id = record.get("robot_id")
1287	            if not isinstance(robot_id, str):
1288	                raise ValueError(f"robot entry {index} field 'robot_id' must be a string")
1289	            if robot_id in robot_ids:
1290	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate robot id {robot_id!r} in checkpoint")
1291	            robot_ids.add(robot_id)
1292	            task_id = record.get("task_id")
1293	            if task_id is not None and not isinstance(task_id, str):
1294	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} field 'task_id' must be a string or null")
1295	            if "position" not in record:
1296	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} is missing field 'position'")
1297	            route = record.get("route")
1298	            if not isinstance(route, list):
1299	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} field 'route' must be a list")
1300	            if "distance_travelled" not in record:
1301	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} is missing field 'distance_travelled'")
1302	            robot_records.append(record)
1303	
1304	        task_records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1305	        task_ids: set[str] = set()
1306	        for index, record in enumerate(raw_tasks):
1307	            if not isinstance(record, dict):
1308	                raise ValueError(f"task entry {index} must be an object")
1309	            task_id = record.get("task_id")
1310	            if not isinstance(task_id, str):
1311	                raise ValueError(f"task entry {index} field 'task_id' must be a string")
1312	            if task_id in task_ids:
1313	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate task id {task_id!r} in checkpoint")
1314	            task_ids.add(task_id)
1315	            assigned = record.get("assigned_robot")
1316	            if assigned is not None and not isinstance(assigned, str):
1317	                raise ValueError(
1318	                    f"task {task_id!r} field 'assigned_robot' must be a string or null"
1319	                )
1320	            if not isinstance(record.get("picked_up"), bool):
1321	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} field 'picked_up' must be a boolean")
1322	            if not isinstance(record.get("completed"), bool):
1323	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} field 'completed' must be a boolean")
1324	            if "pickup" not in record:
1325	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} is missing field 'pickup'")
1326	            if "dropoff" not in record:
1327	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} is missing field 'dropoff'")
1328	            task_records.append(record)
1329	
1330	        positions = [
1331	            tuple(record["position"])
1332	            for record in robot_records
1333	            if isinstance(record["position"], list)
1334	            and len(record["position"]) == 2
1335	            and all(_is_int(value) for value in record["position"])
1336	        ]
1337	        if len(positions) != len(set(positions)):
1338	            raise ValueError("checkpoint robots cannot share a position")
1339	        return robot_records, task_records

1341	    @classmethod
1342	    def _load_change_cells(
1343	        cls, raw: object, context: str, field_name: str
1344	    ) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
1345	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
1346	            raise ValueError(f"{context} field {field_name!r} must be a list")
1347	        cells: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
1348	        for index, cell in enumerate(raw):
1349	            position = _as_pair(cell, f"{context} {field_name} entry {index}")
1350	            cells.append(position)
1351	        return cells

1353	    @classmethod
1354	    def _load_map_changes(cls, data: Mapping[str, object]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
1355	        raw = cls._require_field(data, "map_changes")
1356	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
1357	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'map_changes' must be a list")
1358	        changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1359	        last_tick = -1
1360	        last_sequence = 0
1361	        for index, frame in enumerate(raw):
1362	            context = f"map change {index}"
1363	            if not isinstance(frame, dict):
1364	                raise ValueError(f"{context} must be an object")
1365	            tick = frame.get("tick")
1366	            sequence = frame.get("sequence")
1367	            if not _is_int(tick) or tick < 0:
1368	                raise ValueError(f"{context} field 'tick' must be a non-negative integer")
1369	            if not _is_int(sequence) or sequence <= 0:
1370	                raise ValueError(f"{context} field 'sequence' must be a positive integer")
1371	            if sequence != index + 1:
1372	                raise ValueError(
1373	                    f"map change sequences must run consecutively from 1; change {index} "
1374	                    f"has sequence {sequence}, expected {index + 1}"
1375	                )
1376	            if tick < last_tick:
1377	                raise ValueError(
1378	                    f"{context} tick {tick} is earlier than a preceding map change"
1379	                )
1380	            if tick == last_tick and sequence != last_sequence + 1:
1381	                raise ValueError(f"{context} breaks consecutive sequencing at tick {tick}")
1382	            added = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("added"), context, "added")
1383	            removed = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("removed"), context, "removed")
1384	            if not added and not removed:
1385	                raise ValueError(f"{context} contains no actual obstacle changes")
1386	            overlap = set(added) & set(removed)
1387	            if overlap:
1388	                cell = sorted(overlap)[0]
1389	                raise ValueError(
1390	                    f"{context} adds and removes the same cell {list(cell)}"
1391	                )
1392	            changes.append(
1393	                {
1394	                    "type": "map_change",
1395	                    "tick": tick,
1396	                    "sequence": sequence,
1397	                    "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
1398	                    "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
1399	                }
1400	            )
1401	            last_tick = tick
1402	            last_sequence = sequence
1403	        return changes
